findings.evidence: Page 1 heading order: "6. What Each Command Tells You" → "7. CI Cache Line" → "8. Seven Rules Recap" → callout "A Stack Of Diffs" → "1. Diagnose By Symptom".
findings.fix: Move the "1. Diagnose By Symptom" heading and its Symptom/Likely cause/Move table to the top of page 1, ahead of "6. What Each Command Tells You", so the page reads 1 → 6 → 7 → 8 and ends on the takeaway callout.

findings.summary: The code block under "2. Quick Q" is clipped at its right border, truncating the command mid-path so it renders as a different, destructive command.
findings.evidence: Source text is `RUN apt-get install -y x && rm -rf /var/cache`; the render shows `RUN apt-get install -y x && rm -rf /` with `var/cache` cut off exactly at the dotted box edge, and the question above it reads "Why did the image not shrink after I added rm -rf /var/cache?"
findings.fix: Allow the inline code block to wrap (or reduce its font size / widen the block) so the full `rm -rf /var/cache` argument is visible; non-wrapping single-line code blocks in the left column must fit the ~445px column width.

findings.evidence: Page 1 has "6. What Each Command Tells You" (rows: docker history --no-trunc, dive, docker system df, docker builder prune, build --progress=plain) and "7. CI Cache Line"; page 2 has "6. One-Minute Audit" (lines: docker build --progress=plain, docker history --no-trunc, docker system df, dive) and "7. Mental Model".

findings.summary: The caption's first sentence is a series label rather than a hook, burying the actual hook in sentence two.
findings.evidence: "Part 2 of DOCKER IMAGES: LAYERS, CACHE, LEAN BUILDS. Your 1.1GB Node image and your cache miss on every single push are the same bug..."
findings.fix: Lead with the hook and move the part label to the end: "Your 1.1GB Node image and your cache miss on every single push are the same bug: you put the thing that changes most at the bottom of the stack. ... (Part 2 of DOCKER IMAGES: LAYERS, CACHE, LEAN BUILDS.)"

findings.summary: The advice to `docker run` an intermediate stage ID does not work with BuildKit, which is the default builder in modern Docker and the very builder the surrounding sidebox is about.
findings.evidence: "`docker run --rm -it <stage-id> sh` to poke a stage" — listed under the sidebox titled "buildx Registry Cache"
findings.fix: Replace with the BuildKit-correct workflow: "`docker build --target <stage> -t dbg . && docker run --rm -it dbg sh` to poke a stage" — BuildKit does not emit runnable intermediate image IDs (docker history shows `<missing>` for them).

findings.summary: `BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=1` is described as a determinism/repeatability knob, but it is a cache exporter that embeds cache metadata into the image config for later `--cache-from` reuse.
findings.evidence: "`BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=1` where repeatability matters" — appearing in the same bullet as "`SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` for determinism"
findings.fix: Move it out of the determinism bullet and restate its actual function, e.g. "`--build-arg BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=1` embeds cache metadata in the pushed image so `--cache-from` works without a separate cache ref", and note it is min-mode only (no intermediate stages), unlike the `mode=max` registry cache in section 7.

findings.summary: Heading "3. Quick Q" already appears on page 2.
findings.fix: Rename this section, or merge it with the earlier one.

findings.summary: The apt example that is supposed to model correct same-layer cleanup will fail to build and cleans the wrong directory.
findings.fix: Use `RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends x && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*` — without `apt-get update` there are no package lists on a clean Debian/Ubuntu base and the install fails, and official Debian/Ubuntu images ship a `docker-clean` apt config that already discards `/var/cache/apt/archives`, so removing `/var/cache` reclaims almost nothing; the real weight is `/var/lib/apt/lists`.

findings.summary: The section titled "Seven Rules Recap" lists only five rules.
findings.evidence: "8. Seven Rules Recap" followed by a bullets block with five items ("Order by change frequency..." through "`BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=1` where repeatability matters")
findings.fix: Either retitle to "Five Rules Recap" or restore the two missing rules (the recap of parts 1–2 covers at least seven: layer ordering, same-RUN cleanup, multi-stage, .dockerignore, digest pinning, non-root USER, lockfiles/determinism).

findings.summary: The symptom table lists an error string Docker does not actually emit for a dynamically linked binary on scratch, so readers grepping their logs will not match it.
findings.fix: Use the real messages: `exec /app: no such file or directory` (missing dynamic loader on scratch/distroless-static) or `exec: "sh": executable file not found in $PATH` (no shell in the image).

findings.summary: The handbook's final takeaway is delivered at the end of page 1 while six further sections follow on page 2, so the part appears to conclude twice.
findings.evidence: Page 1 callout: "An image is a cache-friendly stack of diffs. You optimize it by controlling what changes, how often, and at which layer." Page 2 callout: "Every optimization in this handbook answers one question: what changes, how often, and at which layer."
findings.fix: Keep one closing takeaway at the true end of the part (page 2) and replace the page 1 callout with a page-scoped one about inspection and CI cache, or drop it.

findings.summary: `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` and `BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=1` are recommended with no usage example, unlike every other tool in the part which is shown as a runnable command.
findings.evidence: Page 1 bullets: "Commit lockfiles; `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` for determinism" and "`BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=1` where repeatability matters" — no invocation is shown anywhere in the part.
findings.fix: Show the concrete forms alongside the claim, e.g. `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git log -1 --format=%ct) docker buildx build ...` and `docker buildx build --build-arg BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=1 -t repo/app .`, or cut both from the rules recap.
